idea.title: AI receptionist for missed calls at US dental clinics

source.text: An AI receptionist that answers missed calls for US dental clinics and books appointments, $199/month. Launch country US, budget $2,000, 10 hours a week, goal side income, edge: I am a developer. Just go: do not ask questions. Use the slug dental-ai-receptionist.

idea.problem: US dental clinics miss inbound calls (busy front desk, after hours) and lose new-patient appointments.
idea.customer: Independent US dental practices (1-3 dentists, owner-operated) with a front desk that misses calls
idea.solution: An AI voice agent that answers missed and after-hours calls and books appointments.
claims: An AI receptionist that answers missed calls for US dental clinics and books appointments
assumptions: Headless run: the founder asked not to be questioned, so no intake or follow-up questions were asked.
No existing audience, list, network or customers in dentistry (none stated).
No validation done yet (no conversations, waitlist or pre-sales stated).
Booking means writing into the practice management system (Dentrix, Eaglesoft, Open Dental) or a booking layer like NexHealth.
Target is independent practices, not DSOs, since DSOs buy through procurement.

confidence.note: Most demand and churn numbers come from vendors or blogs; CAC to owner-dentists is unverified. 50 real cold contacts would raise it.

gross_margin.note: About 64% on missed-call volume: Retell ~$0.11/min plus NexHealth $0.10 per API call; heavy clinics push cost past $199.

ltv_cac.note: LTV ~$2,700 (4.7% SMB churn) vs CAC ~$1,500 (estimate) gives 1.8.

pricing_power.note: $199 equals Weave's base plan; low-end AI rivals sell at $49-99, so no premium is possible.

build_effort.note: Voice agent on Retell takes days; booking into a PMS plus HIPAA setup takes months at 10 h/week.

skills_match.note: Developer covers the build; healthcare compliance and B2B sales to dentists are missing.

capital_needed.note: Vapi HIPAA add-on $2,000/month and Dentrix write access ~$10,000 exceed the $2,000 budget.

time_to_mvp.note: A demo is fast, a sellable HIPAA-ready booking agent is 2-3 months at 10 h/week (estimate).

sales_cycle.note: Owner-dentist decides, but trust is low: commenters say dentists only trust other dentists.

channel_readiness.note: No audience or network in dentistry; an indie founder reports 600 messages, 0 revenue (R5: no_distribution).

search_demand.note: 205,088 active US dentists, ~135k establishments; missed calls are a known, discussed pain.

trend.note: Funding wave: Patientdesk $1M (2026-02), Linda EUR 2.6M (2026-02), Newton $3.8M (2025-10).

willingness_to_pay.note: Clinics pay $349-1,199/month for Viva AI and $400-1,200/month for human answering.

free_alternatives.note: Weave plans clinics already pay include missed-call text-back; Smith.ai has a free 25-call tier.

competitor_density.note: 12+ named rivals, 3+ YC dental front-desk startups and 10+ launches in 12 months (R3).

differentiation.note: Being a developer is not an edge here; AutoQuill launched at the same $199 (R3).

legal_regulatory.note: Vendor is a HIPAA business associate: BAAs with every clinic and vendor, plus all-party recording consent in 11 states.

platform_dependency.note: Booking needs PMS write access gated by Henry Schein, Patterson or NexHealth, plus a BAA-capable voice vendor.

market_risk.note: Durable need: 62% of dentists name staffing as their top obstacle (ADA HPI, 2025).

skills.note: Strong on the build, no track record selling to clinics or in healthcare compliance.

assets.note: No audience, data, dental network or customers stated.

interest.note: Goal stated as side income; no stated passion for dentistry.

rules_applied.effect: 10+ look-alike launches, no specific edge: competition 2.0 -> 1.5 (competitor_density 2 -> 1, differentiation 2 -> 1.5)

sam.reasoning: TAM x 50% assumed independent (non-DSO) practices that buy without procurement

som.reasoning: 20 clinics x $199 x 12 at 10 h/week, about 0.03% of SAM

competitors_found.reasoning: Named in research: Weave, Arini, Viva, Dentina, Patientdesk, Kairos, Dodo, Peerlogic, Rondah, HelloPatient, Goodcall, Smith.ai

price.reasoning: The founder's stated price; equals Weave's base plan

variable_cost_per_unit.reasoning: 120 missed calls x 3 min x $0.11/min Retell = $40 + 120 x 2 NexHealth API calls x $0.10 = $24 + $2 number + ~$6 card fees

conversion_rate_pct.reasoning: Cold contact to paid clinic, assumed; one indie case had 0 of 600

cac.reasoning: Ads: $8-15 CPC / 2-5% demo rate / 20-30% close = $530-3,750; $1,500 picked in the range

fixed_costs_month.reasoning: Hosting, BAA-capable tiers, compliance tooling, insurance; $2,000+ if Vapi HIPAA add-on is used

break_even_customers_per_month.reasoning: 500 / 127 = 3.9, rounded up; 16 clinics on the Vapi HIPAA path

time_to_first_revenue_weeks.reasoning: 4-6 weeks to a HIPAA-ready pilot at 10 h/week + 2-4 weeks to close a first clinic

verdict.launch_reason: Founder's chosen market; 135k US dental establishments and the price points found are all US.

type_checks.note: SMB SaaS monthly churn 3-7%, median 4.7%: lifetime ~21 months. Normal for the segment, not a killer.
Weave locks clinics with bundled VoIP and 12-month terms, while your product sits on call forwarding: hard to win, easy to lose.

verdict.cheapest_test: 7-day pre-sale: contact 100 independent Open Dental practices and 10 dental marketing agencies, offer a $199 founding pilot (after-hours answer + text summary, no booking).
kill_criteria: Fewer than 5 replies from 100 practice contacts by day 7 -> stop
0 paid pilots or signed letters of intent by day 7 -> stop
No self-serve BAA under $300/month from a voice vendor by day 14 -> stop
More than 50% of prospects already use Weave AI or a rival by day 7 -> stop

rescue.change: Sell a lite after-hours answer + text summary (no PMS booking) at $99-199 to independents
rescue.why: Cuts build_effort, capital_needed and legal surface; keeps the no-channel problem
rescue.requires: Retell or similar with a BAA; 100 practice contacts

rescue.change: Specialise in Open Dental practices only, with real booking via its open API, sold through dental IT providers
rescue.why: Fixes platform_dependency and gives a specific edge that lifts R3
rescue.requires: Open Dental vendor approval; 2-3 dental IT partners

rescue.change: White-label the agent to dental marketing agencies that already serve dentists
rescue.why: Borrows a distribution channel (no_distribution) at the cost of pricing power

narrative.answer: **PIVOT** at 51: dentists will pay for this, but a solo developer has **no channel** to owner-dentists. Funded rivals already sell at your price, and HIPAA plus practice-software access cost more than your budget.
tldr: Demand is real: clinics pay $349-1,199/month for AI receptionists and $400-1,200 for human answering.
The field is crowded and funded: Weave at $199, 3+ YC dental front-desk startups, 10+ look-alike launches in 12 months.
No channel, HIPAA business-associate duties and PMS write access ($10k for Dentrix) make the full product a poor fit for $2,000 and 10 h/week.

key_findings.title: No channel to owner-dentists
key_findings.detail: You have **no dental network**, and an indie founder reports **600 messages, 0 revenue** cold-pitching clinics; dentists mostly trust other dentists.

key_findings.title: Funded rivals already sell your price
key_findings.detail: Weave starts at **$199/month**, Patientdesk raised **$1M from YC** (2026-02), and Arini, Viva and Dentina sell the same job.

key_findings.title: HIPAA and PMS access exceed the budget
key_findings.detail: Vapi's HIPAA add-on is about **$2,000/month** and Dentrix read plus write access about **$10,000**, versus a $2,000 total budget.

narrative.recommendation: Do not build the booking agent. Run a 7-day pre-sale of a lite after-hours answering pilot to 100 Open Dental practices and 10 dental agencies; build only if 2 pay.
narrative.steelman: Missed calls cost a practice an estimated **$15k/month** in production, 75x the price, and staffing shortages are durable. The evidence agrees on the pain; it disagrees that a solo seller can reach buyers before funded rivals.
narrative.lesson: In a funded vertical-AI race, the build is the easy part; the **channel** decides.

premortem.cause: Could not reach owner-dentists: cold emails and calls went unanswered and no peer referral emerged.
premortem.early_signal: Fewer than 5 replies to 100 practice contacts in 7 days

premortem.cause: Prospects already had Weave or a funded AI receptionist and saw no reason to add a second vendor.
premortem.early_signal: More than half of 20 discovery calls mention Weave, Arini or Viva

premortem.cause: HIPAA BAAs and PMS write access cost more time and money than the side project could fund.
premortem.early_signal: No self-serve BAA under $300/month from a voice vendor within 14 days

changes.what: Voice AI platforms dropped to about $0.11/min all-in, making a solo-built agent cheap to run.
FCC ruled AI voices are artificial under the TCPA; outbound recall calls need consent, inbound answering is unaffected.
Patientdesk AI raised $1M from YC for dental front desks.
Linda AI raised EUR 2.6M for dental practice AI workflows.
Kairos Health (YC Fall 2026) went live in 16 US dental locations.

why_now.note: Cheap voice AI opened the window in 2024-2025; by late 2026 funded startups and Weave are **closing it**.

icp.who: Owner-dentist or office manager of an independent 1-3 dentist general practice, 300-500 calls/month, short-staffed front desk
where: Dental marketing agencies and dental IT providers
icp.pays_for_today: Weave phone system $199-399/month; human answering services $400-1,200/month (Viva, 2026-05)
icp.trigger: A front-desk employee quits: 55.4% of dentists hiring admin staff found it very or extremely hard (ADA HPI, 2025)

customer.segment: Independent US general dental practices, 1-3 dentists, not part of a DSO
customer.pain: 30-38% of calls go unanswered in business hours (vendor estimates), losing new patients worth ~$850-1,300 in year one
customer.today: Voicemail, Weave missed-call text-back, human answering services or a funded AI receptionist

use_cases.name: After-hours answering with a text summary to the office
Full booking into Open Dental via its API
White-label agent for dental marketing agencies

free_alternative.evidence: No free tool answers and books dental calls; Weave missed-call text-back and Smith.ai's free 25-call tier cover part of the job.

strong_competitor.evidence: Weave, a public company already on many clinic phones, sells an AI receptionist on top of its $199/month base; Patientdesk raised $1M from YC in 2026-02.

graveyard.evidence: Arini (YC W24) launched as a dental AI receptionist and now sells an operations platform to large healthcare enterprises; indie founders report 600 messages, 0 revenue.

no_distribution.evidence: Founder has no dental audience; Reddit commenters say dentists only trust other dentists and no cold-outreach benchmark for dentists was found.

costs_eat_margin.evidence: On missed-call volume (~360 min/month) cost is ~$72 for a 64% margin; at 900 min/month it reaches $110-285 and the margin can go negative.

weak_demand.evidence: Not hit: 205,088 active US dentists, 62% name staffing as their top obstacle, and funding in dental voice AI rose through 2026.

legal_platform_risk.evidence: The vendor is a HIPAA business associate and needs BAAs across the chain; Dentrix write access reportedly costs ~$10,000 and Twilio's BAA needs an Enterprise edition.

saturated_wave.evidence: At least 10 look-alikes in 12 months: Catchai, AutoQuill ($199), AI Recepts, 0miss, TensorLinks on Product Hunt, Patientdesk and Kairos at YC, and Reddit builder posts.
